chunks: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa narrated to us from 'Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Najran from al-Mufaddal b. Salih from Jabir b. Yazid al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him).

He said: Musa b. 'Imran (peace be upon him) said: O Lord! I am pleased with what You have decreed, yet You cause adults to die and leave behind their young children. So Allah, exalted is His majesty, said: O Musa! Are you not pleased with Me as their Sustainer and Protector? He said: Of course, O Lord! You are the best Trustee, and the best Protector.

key_terms.الوكيل: The Trustee — one entrusted with affairs
key_terms.قضيت: You decreed — referring to God's divine decree (qada')
key_terms.كفيلا: Protector — one who guarantees care and guardianship

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Musa say to Allah about orphaned children in Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration transmitted through Imam al-Baqir (AS), Prophet Musa (AS) questions God about the fate of orphaned children whose parents have died. God reassures Musa that He Himself is their Sustainer and Protector, to which Musa responds with complete trust in God's guardianship. This dialogue reflects the Islamic emphasis on divine providence (rizq) and God's care for the vulnerable, particularly orphans, which was a major concern in pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arabian society.

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (rh) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa narrated to us from `Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Najran from al-Mufaddal b. Salih from Jabir b. Yazid al-Ju`fi from Abi Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali al-Baqir (as).

He said: Musa b. `Imran (as) said: O Lord! I am pleased with what You have decided, but You cause adults to die and leave behind their young children. So, Allah said: O Musa! Are you not pleased with Me as their Sustainer and their Protector? He said: Of course, O Lord. You are the best Trustee and the best Protector.
